**Observations from test image:**
- Soybean leaf with numerous small-medium lesions scattered across the surface
- Lesions have dark brown to purple-black necrotic centers
- Each lesion surrounded by a distinct yellow/chlorotic halo
- Spots are roughly circular, 3-8mm, somewhat irregular

**Analysis:**
The dark necrotic centers with prominent yellow halos are the key discriminating feature. Comparing to Frogeye leaf spot reference: the upper-right panel shows a very similar pattern — dark-centered spots on green leaf with lighter margins, similar size and distribution. Frogeye leaf spot (Cercospora sojina) classically produces circular lesions with dark reddish-brown to purple borders and gray-brown centers, surrounded by chlorotic halos.

The pattern doesn't match Bacterial_Blight (which tends to be more angular/water-soaked) or Septoria brown spot (which has smaller, more irregular brown spots without such distinct halos). Rust would show angular tan lesions with pustules on the underside.
